The link only chooses a directory and fills the prompt box." — nothing reaches the model until the user reads what was filled in and presses Enter. deep-links.md:45 binds the handler's surface: `claude-cli://open` is "the only path the handler accepts", carrying only `q` (prompt prefill, max 5,000 chars), `cwd` and `repo`. deep-links.md:41 binds the disclosure: when the session opens, "a warning line below the input box reads `Prompt from an external link` and stays visible until you send or clear the prompt", with a character count and a scroll-and-review instruction for prompts over 1,000 characters.

divergence: Two deltas, both on the execution half of the page; the directory half already complies. (1) EXECUTION: an OS/web-delivered link is not inert. `send=true` reaches `sendMessage` with no user step (NavigationContext.tsx:753-764), and six further cases in the same switch mutate state (delete-session, delete-source, rename, flag/unflag, set-mode, oauth). The doc's handler accepts one path, `open`; ours accepts any `action/<name>` the switch knows. This is not a wrong key name — the value is honoured and the effect is real. (2) DISCLOSURE: no `Prompt from an external link` warning line exists in any form, so even the non-send prefill path (`onInputChange`) gives the user no signal that the text came from a link, and there is no >1,000-char review notice. Structurally, the missing primitive is an origin distinction: `handleDeepLink` and the `DeepLinkNavigation` DTO carry no `origin`, so the renderer cannot tell an in-app dispatch (EditPopover.tsx:1089, which legitimately needs `send=true`) from an OS or web-page URL. Also out of spec but harmless: the prompt param is `input`, not `q`, and there is no 5,000-char cap.

change.what: Add a required `origin: 'external' | 'internal'` parameter to `handleDeepLink` (:235) — required, not defaulted, so a forgotten call site is a typecheck error rather than a silent trust grant — and stamp it onto the pushed payload at :322-326. Leave the `auth-callback` early return at :111-114 untouched. Fix the stale comment at :48: it says `'new-chat'`; the real action names are the cases in NavigationContext.tsx:676-828.

Add `origin?: 'external' | 'internal'`. Optional keeps an older main process wire-compatible, but the RENDERER must read a missing value as `'external'` — the opposite of the `workspaceId` convention documented two interfaces above at :987-989 ('Missing/null entries always pass the filter'). Say so in the field comment; this is the one place the fail-safe direction can be got backwards.
Pass `origin: 'external'` at all three call sites. One-line each.
Pass `origin: 'external'` — a page rendered in the in-app browser pane is untrusted content, identical in trust to a page in the OS browser.

Thread the origin of the URL that created the window. `handleDeepLink` builds `initialDeepLink` from the incoming URL at deep-link.ts:282-289 when `window=focused|full` is present, so an external link with a window param arrives here; it must stay `'external'` end to end rather than becoming internal by passing through window creation.

This channel currently carries BOTH a trusted in-app click (EditPopover) and an untrusted markdown-link click from model output, so it cannot be labelled internal. Preferred fix: delete the deep-link round-trip from the internal producer — EditPopover.tsx:1081-1101 already has `onCreateSession` and `onSendMessage` in scope and its non-legacy branch at :1075-1077 does exactly that — then hard-code `origin: 'external'` here. Fallback if the legacy branch must keep the URL: add a separate renderer-only channel for internal dispatch and leave `shell.OPEN_URL` external.

Thread origin through `NavigateOptions`, NOT through the route string — the listener re-serialises params into `action/...` at :1102-1111 and any origin put in the query would be indistinguishable from an attacker-supplied param. Then in `handleActionNavigation`, when origin is not `'internal'`: (a) force the prefill branch, i.e. ignore `send === 'true'` at :754 and always take the `onInputChange` path at :765-768; (b) refuse `delete-session` (:780), `delete-source` (:804), `rename-session` (:774), `flag-session`/`unflag-session` (:786/:792), `set-mode` (:810) and `oauth` (:798) — either drop them with a toast or gate each behind an explicit confirm; (c) ignore `mode`, `model` and `systemPrompt` from an external link, or at minimum clamp `mode` so `parsePermissionMode` cannot yield `bypassPermissions` for one; (d) cap `input` length. Keep the existing `workdir` rejection at :685-690 as is.

Render the documented disclosure under the input while an externally seeded prompt is unsent: a line equivalent to `Prompt from an external link`, plus the over-1,000-character variant that shows the count and tells the user to scroll and review. Needs the external flag to travel with the prefill (extend the `onInputChange` path at :765-768 to mark the pending input as external-origin) and to clear on send or clear. Add keys to ALL locale files and keep `lint:i18n:parity` / `lint:i18n:sorted` green.
Add the origin plumbing: an external URL yields a payload stamped `external`, and the existing three client-resolution cases keep passing with the new required parameter.

userImpact: Live and severe today, on three surfaces. A `nessy://action/new-session?input=<attacker text>&send=true` link — on any web page, in a Slack/wiki message, in a page opened in Nessy's own browser pane, or rendered as a markdown link inside an assistant message — creates a session on one click and sends the attacker's prompt to the model roughly 100 ms later. The user sees a new chat appear with a message they did not write, already being answered; there is no confirmation, no `Prompt from an external link` warning, and nothing to cancel before the turn starts. The same link can set the new session's permission mode, and `parsePermissionMode` accepts `bypassPermissions` (also spelled `allowall` or `execute`), so the auto-sent prompt can run in the mode that does not ask before tool use. Sibling links are destructive without any prompt at all: `nessy://action/delete-session/<id>` deletes a session, `nessy://action/delete-source/<id>` removes a source, `nessy://action/set-mode/<sessionId>?mode=bypassPermissions` flips an existing session out of its permission mode, and `nessy://action/oauth/<sourceSlug>` starts a sign-in flow. Session ids are guessable enough for a shotgun link, and the markdown-link surface means model output that quotes a fetched web page is itself a delivery path. Nothing in the UI distinguishes any of this from a link the user's own app generated.
